_meta.indication: ORILISSA is a GnRH receptor antagonist indicated for the management of moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis.

pivotal_trials.design: Six-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multinational trial
pivotal_trials.population: Premenopausal women with moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: proportion of subjects whose dysmenorrhea responded to treatment at Month 3 and proportion whose non-menstrual pelvic pain responded to treatment at Month 3
pivotal_trials.n: Study EM-1: 150 mg N=248, 200 mg N=244, placebo N=373
pivotal_trials.result: Study EM-1 dysmenorrhea responders: 46% (150 mg) and 76% (200 mg) vs 20% placebo; non-menstrual pelvic pain responders: 50% (150 mg) and 55% (200 mg) vs 36% placebo (both doses superior to placebo on both co-primary endpoints)

pivotal_trials.design: Six-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multinational trial
pivotal_trials.population: Premenopausal women with moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: proportion of subjects whose dysmenorrhea responded at Month 3 and proportion whose non-menstrual pelvic pain responded at Month 3
pivotal_trials.n: Study EM-2: 150 mg N=221, 200 mg N=225, placebo N=353
pivotal_trials.result: Study EM-2 dysmenorrhea responders: 43% (150 mg) and 72% (200 mg) vs 23% placebo; non-menstrual pelvic pain responders: 50% (150 mg) and 58% (200 mg) vs 37% placebo (both doses superior to placebo on both co-primary endpoints)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>5%) were hot flush or night sweats (24% at 150 mg, 46% at 200 mg vs 9% placebo), headache (17%, 20% vs 12%), nausea (11%, 16% vs 13%) and insomnia (6%, 9% vs 3%). Notable risks include bone mineral density loss, dose-dependent ALT elevations, and depression/suicidal ideation and behavior.
target_moa: Elagolix is a nonpeptide GnRH receptor antagonist that binds reversibly with high affinity to the human GnRH receptor and reduces pituitary secretion of LH and FSH, causing dose-dependent suppression of estradiol and progesterone.
modality: Small molecule (oral nonpeptide GnRH receptor antagonist)

rems.type: No REMS required; potential risks can be adequately managed through product labeling alone.

companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic issues; not applicable.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; the Division determined the NDA did not raise issues requiring external expert advice.

description.text: Labeling revision to reflect drug-drug interaction study of elagolix 200mg twice daily co-administered with a combined oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel)

citations.quote: Revisions to reflect the results of Study M18-980, a drug-drug interaction (DDI) study to assess the co-administration of a combined oral contraceptive (containing ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel) with elagolix 200mg twice daily. Study M18-890 also addressed postmarketing requirement (PMR) 3390-3.

basis.text: Priority Review granted because elagolix treats a serious condition (endometriosis with associated pain) and provides a significant improvement in safety compared to available therapies such as opioids.

citations.quote: The NDA was submitted on August 23, 2017, with a request for Priority Review because elagolix will treat a serious condition (endometriosis with associated pain) and provide a significant improvement in safety compared to available therapies, such as opioids.

summary.text: Orilissa (elagolix), a new molecular entity, received full (traditional) approval under a Priority Review of NDA 210450, submitted August 23, 2017, based on two Phase 3 placebo-controlled trials; no advisory committee was convened and no REMS was required.

citations.quote: The NDA was submitted on August 23, 2017, with a request for Priority Review because elagolix will treat a serious condition (endometriosis with associated pain) and provide a significant improvement in safety compared to available therapies, such as opioids.

The Applicant evaluated the efficacy of Orilissa in two Phase 3 trials (Studies 665 and 671) that randomized a total of 1686 premenopausal women with moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis to Orilissa (475 received 150 mg once daily and 477 received 200 mg twice daily) or placebo.
The Division determined that the NDA did not raise issues requiring external expert advice. Therefore, an advisory committee meeting was not convened to discuss the application.

requirement.text: 3390-3: A drug-drug interaction trial to assess the pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability of co-administration of a combined oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel) with Orilissa 200 mg twice daily.

citations.quote: 3390-3 A drug-drug interaction trial to assess the pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability of the co-administration of a combined oral contraceptive (containing ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel) with Oritelissa 200 mg twice daily.

requirement.text: 3390-4: A randomized, controlled clinical trial to assess the effects of a combined hormonal contraceptive on the efficacy of Orilissa in women with moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis, and effects of Orilissa on the contraceptive's efficacy and safety with concomitant use.

citations.quote: 3390-4 A randomized, controlled clinical trial to assess the effects of a combined hormonal contraceptive on the efficacy of Orilissa in women with moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis. This trial will also assess the effects of Orilissa on the efficacy of the combined hormonal contraceptive, and safety with concomitant use of Orilissa and the combined hormonal contraceptive.
